name: Brown-Teitelboim Membrane Bubble
description: A spherical charged membrane joins two regions of de Sitter space with different cosmological constants.
history: A spherical membrane separates two regions of de Sitter space, each with its own cosmological constant. In the decay, the constant is smaller inside the bubble, and the membrane expands after it appears [hirano2018bt, brown1987neutralization, brown1988membrane]. J. David Brown and Claudio Teitelboim proposed this mechanism of cosmological constant neutralization in 1987 and developed it in 1988 [hirano2018bt, brown1987neutralization, brown1988membrane].¶In units with $c=1$, static coordinates on either side of the membrane have the line element $$ds_{i,o}^2=-f_{i,o}(r)dt_{i,o}^2+\frac{dr^2}{f_{i,o}(r)}+r^2d\Omega_2^2,\qquad f_{i,o}(r)=1-\frac{\Lambda_{i,o}r^2}{3},$$ where $i$ and $o$ mark the inside and outside, $r$ is the areal radius, and $d\Omega_2^2=d\theta^2+\sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2$ [hirano2018bt]. The two time coordinates need not agree across the wall, and each static chart covers the region where its $f$ is positive. The membrane's own radius is $r=R(\tau)$, with $\tau$ its proper time. Its induced geometry is continuous across the wall, and its tension bends the two sides differently [hirano2018bt].¶The jump in extrinsic curvature obeys Werner Israel's junction condition $$K_{ab}(o)-K_{ab}(i)=4\pi G\sigma\,h_{ab},$$ where $h_{ab}$ is the induced metric, $\sigma$ is the membrane tension, $G$ is Newton's constant, and $K_{ab}$ uses $K_{ab}=-\tfrac12(\nabla_a n_b+\nabla_b n_a)$ with a common unit normal $n$ directed from inside to outside and indices projected onto the wall [hirano2018bt, israel1966]. Together with continuity of $h_{ab}$ and the two cosmological constants, this condition fixes the allowed membrane radius and its motion through the two geometries [hirano2018bt]. The wall has the geometry of a three dimensional de Sitter space: its radius starts at a minimum and grows as proper time advances [hirano2018bt].¶The membrane carries the charge $q$ of a field whose strength has four antisymmetric indices [hirano2018bt, brown1987neutralization, brown1988membrane]. In four dimensions this four form is a constant $E$ times the spacetime volume form on each side, and its energy contributes to the cosmological constant [bousso2000flux, hirano2018bt]. Across the charged membrane $E$ jumps by the charge, $E_i=E_o-q$, so the effective cosmological constant changes as well [hirano2018bt]. The difference is $\Lambda_i-\Lambda_o=-8\pi Gq(E_o-q/2)$, so $q(E_o-q/2)>0$ makes the inside value smaller [hirano2018bt]. An upward change is also possible [bousso2000flux]. Upward jumps from a de Sitter parent vacuum are more strongly suppressed than downward jumps [bousso2000flux].¶Jaume Garriga calculated the fluctuation prefactors for charged membrane nucleation in flat and de Sitter backgrounds in 1994 [garriga1994rates]. The membrane displacements act as a scalar field on the spherical Euclidean world volume, whose fluctuation determinant supplies the prefactor [garriga1994rates]. Garriga treated the gravitational field and the four form as external and proposed a stationary distribution of bubble sizes in de Sitter space [garriga1994rates].¶Raphael Bousso and Andrew Chamblin coupled charged membranes to an inflaton in 1999 [bousso1999open]. They constructed regular instantons joining two regions of open inflation across a membrane [bousso1999open]. The inflaton coupling removes the singular pole of the instanton; the four form contributes negatively to the vacuum energy in the convention used for these instantons [bousso1999open].¶Raphael Bousso and Joseph Polchinski extended the mechanism to several four forms in 2000 [bousso2000flux]. Their quantized fluxes can furnish a closely spaced set of possible cosmological constants, and multiple fluxes arise in compactifications of M theory [bousso2000flux]. Membranes change the fluxes in steps, allowing different regions to occupy different values in that set [bousso2000flux].¶Jonathan Lee Feng and coauthors examined the nucleation of coincident branes in 2001 [feng2001saltatory]. Feng and coauthors estimated a large enhancement of the nucleation probability from internal states of the coincident branes [feng2001saltatory]. Feng and coauthors evaluated the enhancement using the ambient de Sitter temperature or the geometric mean of the temperatures before and after nucleation [feng2001saltatory]. Jaume Garriga and Alexander Vilenkin argued that the degeneracy factor is insensitive to the ambient de Sitter temperature and can enhance or suppress nucleation, depending on the fields on the brane [garriga2001solutions].¶Gia Dvali and Vilenkin constructed solitonic membranes whose charge is suppressed by a broken discrete symmetry in 2001 [dvali2001field]. The charge contains a power of the ratio of the symmetry breaking scale to the ultraviolet cutoff, allowing closely spaced vacuum energies [dvali2001field]. After eliminating the four form, the coupled scalar has a periodic potential with an additional quadratic term [dvali2001field].¶Garriga and Ariel Megevand examined the forces between coincident branes after moduli stabilization in 2004 [garriga2004coincident]. The long range gravitational and four form forces repel the branes; a spherical coincident instanton requires attraction at short distances to hold the stack together [garriga2004coincident]. They also constructed a static instanton for the pair creation of critical bubbles, whose nucleation rate depends exponentially on the ambient de Sitter temperature [garriga2004coincident].¶Andrés Gomberoff, Marc Henneaux, Claudio Teitelboim, and Frank Wilczek examined thermal production of charged membranes by a cosmological horizon in 2004 [gomberoff2004thermal]. The unstable static membrane configuration, the cosmological thermalon, can lower the cosmological constant as the membrane collapses into a black hole [gomberoff2004thermal]. This decay channel depends on gravity and disappears when Newton's constant tends to zero [gomberoff2004thermal]. Garriga and Megevand found larger decay exponents for the static seed and remnant channels than for tunneling between the same two vacua under the boundary conditions used in that comparison [garriga2004activation].¶Michal Fabinger and Eva Silverstein analyzed the causal structure and thermodynamics of de Sitter regions joined across D-brane walls in 2004 [fabinger2004dsitter]. Observers at a fixed distance from the wall have static causal patches, and a detector moving with the wall measures a temperature set by the intrinsic de Sitter radius of the wall [fabinger2004dsitter]. They compared the entropy carried by the branes with the parent horizon entropy and found matching dependence on the flux in a string scale limit, up to factors of order one [fabinger2004dsitter].¶Senarath P. de Alwis compared the membrane tension with the local string and Kaluza-Klein scales in stabilized type IIB compactifications in 2007 [dealwis2007scales]. Wrapped branes in the examples have a tension above the cube of the local string scale, even when the vacua on both sides admit a supergravity description [dealwis2007scales]. Senarath P. de Alwis questioned a low energy supergravity calculation of the nucleation dynamics in those examples [dealwis2007scales].¶Stefano Ansoldi and Lorenzo Sindoni calculated semiclassical tunneling amplitudes for spherical tension shells joining de Sitter or anti-de Sitter regions in 2007 [ansoldi2007shell]. They reproduced the thin wall decay exponent in four dimensions and classified the causal structures of the joined regions [ansoldi2007shell]. They interpreted the initial state by assuming a change in the shell stress tensor at small radius [ansoldi2007shell].¶Jose Juan Blanco-Pillado and coauthors constructed flux changing bubble instantons in a six dimensional Einstein-Maxwell compactification in 2009 [blanco2009tunneling]. Magnetic flux through the compact sphere stabilizes its radius, and a magnetically charged brane lowers the flux as a bubble expands [blanco2009tunneling]. The reduced four dimensional description contains a charged membrane and the scalar that measures the size of the compact space [blanco2009tunneling].¶Adam R. Brown and Alex Dahlen allowed the radius of the compact space to change near the membrane in 2010 [brown2010steps]. The enlarged internal space lowers the effective tension of a brane stack and can favor jumps across several flux values [brown2010steps]. They demonstrated this effect in the thin wall approximation to a six dimensional Einstein-Maxwell compactification, with the shape of the compact space held fixed [brown2010steps].¶Adam R. Brown and Alex Dahlen examined bubbles that discharge several fluxes together in 2011 [brown2011giant]. The branes that discharge different fluxes can bind, reducing the tension of the combined membrane [brown2011giant]. For low curvature parent vacua in the thin brane models, transitions across several flux values can dominate the decay [brown2011giant].¶Matthew Kleban and coauthors examined flux discharge when a compact dimension is larger than the nucleated bubble in 2011 [kleban2011cascade]. An expanding membrane can pass through itself after circling the compact direction and discharge further units of flux at each crossing [kleban2011cascade]. They followed this cascade with gravitational backreaction neglected, so its continuation after a large fraction of the flux has discharged requires a gravitational treatment [kleban2011cascade].¶Guido D’Amico and coauthors used the flux cascade to drive inflation inside a nucleated bubble in 2013 [damico2013unwinding]. Repeated membrane crossings reduce the vacuum energy, and annihilation of the membrane with an oppositely oriented copy can end inflation and produce radiation [damico2013unwinding]. They calculated density perturbations in effective descriptions with stabilized compact dimensions; a complete stabilized string construction remained open [damico2013unwinding].¶Jon Brown and coauthors calculated membrane transitions between branches of an axion potential in 2016 [brown2016monodromy]. The rolling axion contributes kinetic energy outside the bubble, changing the decay exponent from the estimate for a transition between stationary vacua [brown2016monodromy]. They evaluated the exponent with gravity neglected and identified regimes in which the stationary vacuum estimate has the same parameter dependence [brown2016monodromy].¶Shinji Hirano related the membrane nucleation action to horizon thermodynamics in 2018 [hirano2018bt]. The de Sitter decay exponent contains the change in horizon entropy and the change in redshifted energy [hirano2018bt]. The gravitational contribution to the membrane radius also changes the critical flux below which an anti-de Sitter vacuum resists further membrane nucleation [hirano2018bt].¶Gian Francesco Giudice and coauthors coupled the Higgs to a four form in a cosmological selection model in 2019 [giudice2019higgs]. Charged membranes change both the vacuum energy and the Higgs mass, with a membrane charge chosen to set the electroweak scale [giudice2019higgs]. Nemanja Kaloper and Alexander Westphal developed a related Higgs flux landscape in 2020 [kaloper2020higgs]. Vacuum selection depends on additional cosmological and anthropic assumptions in these models [giudice2019higgs, kaloper2020higgs].¶Senarath P. de Alwis and coauthors calculated semiclassical transition probabilities for spherical walls joining Minkowski and de Sitter regions in 2020 [dealwis2020transitions]. The zero mass limit of a Schwarzschild background retains a finite upward amplitude under a prescription based on the entropy of the background state [dealwis2020transitions]. They recovered the de Sitter entropy ratio with the Hartle-Hawking branch of the wave function; relative probabilities alone do not determine a decay time [dealwis2020transitions].¶Alek Bedroya and coauthors averaged a sequence of membrane discharges into effective scalar evolution in 2020 [bedroya2020bubbles]. They constrained the membrane tensions and vacuum energy steps using the weak gravity and trans-Planckian censorship conjectures [bedroya2020bubbles]. They assumed thin walls, small changes between positive vacuum energies and a state with a finite bubble crossing rate [bedroya2020bubbles].¶Fotis Farakos and coauthors coupled a membrane to a nilpotent three form multiplet in de Sitter supergravity in 2021 [farakos2021goldstino]. A flux jump can remove the goldstino multiplet, which contains the fermion associated with broken supersymmetry, and leave a supersymmetric anti-de Sitter interior [farakos2021goldstino]. A short decay time requires an assumed hierarchy between membrane charge and tension; larger tensions can suppress the transition [farakos2021goldstino].¶Sebastián Céspedes and coauthors examined the Lorentzian evolution of joined de Sitter regions in 2021 [cespedes2021slicing]. They recovered the expanding hyperboloid trajectory of the wall and proposed a description with closed spatial slices [cespedes2021slicing]. They left the treatment of quantum wall fluctuations and the scalar field dynamics beyond the thin wall approximation open [cespedes2021slicing].¶Nemanja Kaloper promoted the cosmological constant and Planck mass to variables that jump at charged membranes in 2022 [kaloper2022hidden, kaloper2022general]. The flux contribution to the vacuum energy is linear in that construction [kaloper2022hidden, kaloper2022general]. Kaloper and Alexander Westphal also examined a version with a fixed Planck mass and two irrationally related membrane charges [kaloper2022quantum]. Those charges allow densely spaced vacuum energies [kaloper2022quantum]. The decay exponent diverges toward a Minkowski parent on the positive tension branch with both Euclidean de Sitter regions smaller than a hemisphere [kaloper2022quantum].¶Maite Arcos and coauthors calculated membrane nucleation rates at strong coupling using holography in 2022 [arcos2022holography]. They obtained the decay exponent from a membrane in anti-de Sitter space ending on a surface with a flat or de Sitter metric [arcos2022holography]. The gravitational field and the antisymmetric form field remain external in this calculation [arcos2022holography].¶Ulf Danielsson and coauthors constructed charged shells with an anti-de Sitter interior in 2022 [danielsson2022shells]. Wrapped D3 branes expand into spherical five branes, and Coulomb repulsion can hold the shell at a finite radius [danielsson2022shells]. They assumed a warped string compactification with an antibrane uplift and a small vacuum energy difference across the shell; the exterior has a Reissner-Nordström geometry [danielsson2022shells].¶Kaloper extended the decay analysis to more general flux actions in 2023 [kaloper2023decay]. A linear flux contribution controls the same small curvature suppression when it dominates the terms with higher powers of flux [kaloper2023decay]. Kaloper also held a heavy axion at a local minimum and discharged the remaining flux by membranes [kaloper2023axion]. Restrictions on the allowed field and flux ranges leave a finite set of vacuum energies and a nonzero gap from zero in that construction [kaloper2023axion].¶Yang Liu and coauthors studied membrane transitions with several four forms and scalar fields in 2023 [liu2023zero]. They identified bounds on the membrane charges and tensions under which the decay rate vanishes as the parent vacuum approaches Minkowski space [liu2023zero]. Nearby de Sitter vacua can then remain long lived [liu2023zero].¶Igor Bandos and coauthors calculated charged membrane nucleation in theories with scalar fields and supersymmetry in 2023 [bandos2023nucleation]. Small explicit supersymmetry breaking terms allow the higher energy vacuum to decay through spherical membranes [bandos2023nucleation]. They found numerical de Sitter to anti-de Sitter bubbles with the scalar field and metric responding to the membrane, without a thin wall approximation for those profiles [bandos2023nucleation].¶Nemanja Kaloper and Alexander Westphal examined limits set by the membrane weak gravity conjecture in 2024 [kaloper2024weak]. Membranes with charge and tension satisfying that conjecture provide decay channels for de Sitter vacua [kaloper2024weak]. The low curvature decay rate depends on whether linear or quadratic flux terms dominate [kaloper2024weak].¶Ansoldi and Takahiro Tanaka examined quantum fluctuations during upward de Sitter bubble tunneling in 2024 [ansoldi2024fluctuations]. The Euclidean lapse changes sign along the chosen path, and a Gaussian fluctuation wave function becomes nonnormalizable [ansoldi2024fluctuations]. They left open whether a treatment beyond that construction preserves the usual instanton exponent [ansoldi2024fluctuations].¶Céspedes and coauthors calculated Hamiltonian transition probabilities between joined de Sitter, Minkowski and anti-de Sitter regions in 2024 [cespedes2024transitions]. De Sitter transitions obey detailed balance with the Hartle-Hawking choice of wave function [cespedes2024transitions]. Upward transitions from Minkowski and anti-de Sitter regions have a finite amplitude under a prescription that assigns zero entropy to each empty background [cespedes2024transitions]. They imposed spherical symmetry and the thin wall approximation; the amplitude alone does not supply a decay time or a fluctuation prefactor [cespedes2024transitions].¶Min-Seok Seo examined flux discharge in the six dimensional Einstein-Maxwell compactification in 2024 [seo2024tower]. The membrane changes the magnetic flux through the compact sphere and leaves the six dimensional cosmological constant fixed [seo2024tower]. Along this transition, a tower of Kaluza-Klein states does not descend to zero mass at the four dimensional Minkowski vacuum, so that tower does not obstruct the discharge [seo2024tower].¶Liu and coauthors examined the membrane weak gravity conjecture in 2024 [liu2024weak]. Minkowski space can be stable under membrane nucleation in a generalized Dirac-Born-Infeld theory when the membrane parameters satisfy the conjecture [liu2024weak]. The four form energy is quadratic in the flux at small values and approaches a linear dependence on its magnitude at large values [liu2024weak].¶Kaloper proposed a hidden confining gauge sector whose four form supplies a transient dark energy density in 2025 [kaloper2025evanescent]. Charged membranes discharge the flux in discrete steps and reduce the vacuum energy inside expanding bubbles [kaloper2025evanescent]. Kaloper chose the membrane charge and tension so that the decay becomes appreciable on the scale of the present cosmic age, using bubbles much smaller than the cosmological horizon [kaloper2025evanescent].¶Priyesh Chakraborty and coauthors used charged membrane nucleation to switch off an axion mass in 2026 [chakraborty2026axion]. The membrane changes an integer flux that controls a coupling between two three forms, allowing the axion to be heavy during inflation and suppressing large scale isocurvature fluctuations [chakraborty2026axion]. They assumed a time dependent membrane tension so that the bubbles percolate [chakraborty2026axion].¶Anastasios Irakleous and coauthors proposed a holographic description of the joined de Sitter regions in 2026 [irakleous2026bubble]. They assigned degrees of freedom to two screens on the cosmological horizons and calculated entanglement entropies from constrained extremal surfaces [irakleous2026bubble]. For the positive tension branches, the leading entropy does not exceed the horizon entropy of the parent de Sitter region [irakleous2026bubble].¶James Halverson, Justin Khoury, and Cody Long studied membrane transitions in a modified flux model motivated by type IIB and F theory compactifications in 2026 [halverson2026vacuum]. They found that transitions across many flux values dominate in an approximation of thin probe branes with gravitational corrections neglected [halverson2026vacuum]. They also found a necessary bound on the ratio of the number of fluxes to the Euler characteristic of the compact space from the lifetime of a low energy vacuum [halverson2026vacuum].¶Kaloper coupled the charged membranes to electromagnetism through a Chern-Simons interaction in 2026 [kaloper2026em, kaloper2026cmb]. A photon crossing the wall acquires a polarization rotation set by the flux jump, with no frequency dependence below the effective cutoff in the sharp wall approximation [kaloper2026cmb]. Kaloper calculated the transmitted and reflected waves and recovered the earlier weak coupling rotation as the leading term [kaloper2026em, kaloper2026cmb].¶Kaloper coupled visible and dark electromagnetism to the flux jump in 2026 [kaloper2026darkphotons]. Light crossing a membrane can then convert into dark photons through a Chern-Simons coupling of the two gauge fields to the four form [kaloper2026darkphotons]. Kaloper treated a locally planar thin wall with weak couplings and no incident dark radiation, at frequencies below the cutoff of the top form sector [kaloper2026darkphotons].¶Muhammad Ghulam Khuwajah Khan added a magnetic monopole flux on the membrane world volume in 2026 [khan2026topolons]. For an interior vacuum energy at least as large as the exterior value, the spherical membrane has a finite nonzero energy as its radius tends to zero in the static Dirac-Born-Infeld description [khan2026topolons]. The collapsed core and its gravitational field require physics beyond that effective description [khan2026topolons].¶Thibaut Coudarchet and coauthors studied bubbles nucleating at late global time in de Sitter space in 2026 [coudarchet2026lorentzian]. They recovered the Euclidean membrane decay exponent from a Hamiltonian treatment of the membrane radius [coudarchet2026lorentzian]. Upward bubbles and downward bubbles with sufficiently large tension reach the parent cosmological horizon before classical motion becomes allowed in the spherical thin wall approximation [coudarchet2026lorentzian].

related.text: A bubble of lower vacuum energy bounded by a wall, here a charged membrane that changes a four form across it [hirano2018bt, bousso2000flux].
The geometry on each side of the membrane, with a different cosmological constant inside and outside [hirano2018bt].
A gravitating wall with flat spacetime on both sides, carrying no charge and no change in the cosmological constant [hirano2018bt, caldwell1996].

coordinates.name: Static, Inside the Membrane

parameters.description: Positive cosmological constant inside the membrane, an inverse length squared
Areal radius of the membrane in the static time of this region

coordinates.convention: We use static coordinates $(t,r,\theta,\phi)$ inside the membrane, with $t$ the static time and $r$ the areal radius. The wall sits at $r=r_w(t)$. A dot in a geodesic is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter.

coordinates.name: de Sitter Slices, Inside the Membrane

parameters.description: de Sitter radius on this side, $\ell_i = \sqrt{3/\Lambda_i}$
The value of $\chi$ at the membrane on this side

coordinates.convention: We use the de Sitter slices $(\eta,\chi,\theta,\phi)$ inside the membrane. The membrane sits at $\chi=\chi_i$, and $\eta$ is dimensionless. A dot in a geodesic is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter.

parameters.description: The de Sitter radius inside the membrane
The minimum areal radius of the membrane

coordinates.convention: The coordinate $\tau$ is the membrane proper time extended along the de Sitter slices, and $r$ is the areal radius. The wall sits at $r=R_0\cosh(\tau/R_0)$. A dot in a geodesic is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter.
